@graph.name: Elenchon WPS Manager — Welding Heat Input Calculator
@graph.description: A live welding heat input calculator that clamps every control to your PQR-qualified range. Set the root, fill and cap windows, drag current, voltage and travel-speed sliders, and see heat input computed live in kJ — multi-arc aware for tandem and twin setups, and it loads per-region ranges straight from a parsed WPS.

Sliders clamped to the PQR-qualified range — out-of-range values not dialable

mainEntity.name: How does the calculator work out heat input?

acceptedAnswer.text: It computes heat input live from the arc parameters — current, voltage and travel speed — as you drag the sliders, showing the result in kJ for the weld region you're working. Root, fill and cap each have their own qualified range.

mainEntity.name: Can it stop me from going out of qualification?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — that's the point. The sliders clamp to your PQR-qualified range, so you physically can't dial in a combination whose heat input falls outside what the procedure allows. Leaving the window isn't possible, rather than flagged after the fact.

mainEntity.name: Does it handle tandem or twin-arc welding?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Tandem and twin-arc setups get a lead head and a trail head, each with its own current and voltage, and the total heat input is summed across the heads the way the standard expects — checked against the same qualified window.

mainEntity.name: Do I have to type in the qualified ranges?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can, or you can load a parsed WPS from your library and its per-region ranges and processes fill in automatically. The ranges come from the WPS; the arc parameters stay yours to explore.

mainEntity.name: Does it save what I calculate?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. It's a scratch pad — a live calculation surface. Nothing you do here is saved or written to any sheet or register, so you can explore freely without changing anything.

mainEntity.name: Is heat input qualified per region?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The helper sets and checks root, fill and cap separately, because that's how a PQR qualifies heat input — region by region, each against its own limits.
